CursorTimucua Gold · 15%
Risk Sixteen unraced horses means trial strength and yard tactics are largely hidden, so a co-favourite can easily underperform.
official ratings or trial benchmarksconfirmed pacemaker/split intentions from Murtagh and A P O'Brienearly pace map and whether high draws get a clear run in a 16-runner break
Timucua Gold gets the nod on connections and track geometry rather than the 1.1 quote. W J Lee is the strongest jockey on the card by recent strike rate, Noel Meade’s yard is a solid maiden source, and draw 13 sits in the high third where Curragh 7f winners have clustered (43% over the sample). That is a modest edge in a wide-open debut, not proof he wins.

The main danger is the race shape itself: with no exposed form, any of A P O’Brien’s pair (Noble Exhibit from a high draw with the main yard’s debut record), Kokoshanelle’s extra 5lb suggesting superior homework, or one of J P Murtagh’s four could prove stronger once the pace settles. A short price here is context only — in a 16-runner maiden the true chance for even the best candidate stays in the mid-teens.

CursorNO BET · 38%
Risk Five unraced debutants in seven leave more than half the field as complete unknowns despite Silent Sadhu’s exposed run.
Official ratings on the debutsRichard Spencer’s intended target between his two runnersPace map — who leads and whether Sadhu gets a soft lead at six furlongs
Silent Sadhu is the logical form pick, not because of 1.1. His Newbury six-furlong Good To Firm Class 2 effort — beaten a nose from a huge price in an eighteen-runner — is the clearest speed-and-stamina evidence in the race, and he has already proven he handles this trip and ground. That still leaves him winless in two starts, with a weaker Ascot follow-up, and in a seven-runner Class 4 with five debuts the true win chance is nowhere near the market’s implied ninety-plus percent; I put him around 38%, well ahead of the rest on known data alone.

Walkin On The Moon is the main danger on racecourse knowledge: he has already run at Newmarket (July) and has twice been beaten narrowly at big prices, which fits a horse still finding his level rather than one without talent. Draw one is a minor negative on the published six-furlong bias (low third of stalls underperform high), and Spencer also saddling Great Balls O'Fire adds setup uncertainty. I would not stake the race at Sadhu’s price or with this much unraced ambiguity; the likeliest winner on form is Sadhu, but the edge is poor and the debuts are the bigger structural risk.

CursorSaxony Charms · 17%
Risk Draw 3 fights the Curragh 10f high-draw lean, and the pace tag plus 57-day break may mean a support role rather than full win intent.
Official ratings for most of the fieldConfirmed pacemaker plan (Handani and Saxony Charms both flagged)Early pace map at 10f on Good To Firm
Saxony Charms has the strongest course-and-distance evidence in the race: fifth of eleven at this exact Curragh 10f Good-to-Firm test, beaten only a neck, off a prior third over the same trip here. That is materially sharper local form than Will You Stop’s respectable fourth, beaten a length, and better than the Leopardstown form of Handani and Let’s Smash It, which has not been replicated over ten furlongs. W J Lee is the standout jockey on the card by six-month numbers, and Oliver’s runner looks purposefully rerouted back to the scene of that near-miss rather than thrown in blindly.

The main reservation is race geometry and yard tactics, not ability on paper. High draws have won disproportionately at Curragh around this trip, which hurts Saxony Charms from three, while Acula (14), Sunatia (13), and several others sit where the bias is friendlier. Weld’s Handani is a live improver and may take the race forward; if Saxony Charms is asked to assist pace, her true win chance drops sharply despite the form line. Will You Stop is the safer alternative: OR 80, proven ten-furlong Curragh form, and Slattery’s solid recent strike-rate give him a more draw-neutral path to contention if…

CursorPlayful Fox · 30%
Risk An earlier unseated run means jumping must stay clean over 17f on a track where completion matters.
Official ratings for unrated runnersNewton Abbot course form for the main contendersEarly pace and whether King's Scholar's 86-day break has left him short of peak fitness
Playful Fox is the most reliable form horse in the field: a Good-ground win at Stratford on firm-ish ground, then a solid second at Worcester 31 days ago, trained by the card’s strongest yard and ridden by Harry Skelton. At 17f on Good To Firm he maps well off 16f–20f runs, carries a workable mark (OR 102) against mainly unknown or weakly exposed rivals, and has completed cleanly in his last three starts despite an older “U” in the form string. King’s Scholar has the best official rating and two convincing C4 wins before a long break, but 86 days off, no Newton Abbot form, and a 10lb claimer instead of a senior jockey cap his true win chance below the market’s likely respect for the topweight.

The biggest risk to Playful Fox is jumping consistency in a small field where one mistake can be costly; Lundy View’s 39L defeat here suggests the track can expose poor jumpers, and Whermyrosemarygoes is the unexposed danger if her Uttoxeter debut win translates to this trip with Cobden aboard. If King’s Scholar returns fit despite the layoff, his class could override Playful Fox’s current-condition edge.

Ealu Tapa is the most condition-aligned profile: he has actually won over hurdles at ~16f on Good (Ballinrobe 1/13), giving him a concrete ceiling the market cannot manufacture. Sea Eagle is the main danger — fresher (15 days), more experienced, and a close second at Wexford 17f Good — but his career includes unseats and he is still searching for a second hurdle win. Minella Moon Shine (Good-ground placings) and Cast A Cold Eye (Mullins, respectable debut) are live improvers, while Ikalimix’s OR 95 is offset by a Cork fall on Good last time.

The biggest risk to Ealu Tapa is translation: this is an 18-runner puzzle with many unrated or lightly raced rivals, so a proven Good-ground winner elsewhere does not guarantee Killarney suitability, and a wide-open pace could flatter a hold-up type like Sea Eagle instead.

confirmed pace map with Balding's two runnersLazy Griff's Goodwood 40L flop explanationexact Chester 14.5f draw bias for 8 runners on GTS
Orchard Keeper is the most convincing profile for this exact test: fourth of six here last August over 14f on good ground in Class 1, beaten only half a length, with a 1–4 distance record and repeated close placings at around this trip (Bath 14f, Newmarket July). Roger Varian's runner arrives off a sensible 21-day break, carries a useful 5 lb claim, and does not rely on a short price to prove stamina — unlike the joint market leaders.

The main threat is By The Book: Billy Loughnane is the card's top-ranked jockey and the horse is clearly talented, but three runs all at 12f or under make 14.5f Chester a major unknown at 3.1; Lazy Griff tops the weights on OR 113 but the Goodwood collapse and a poor jockey strike-rate cap confidence. I disagree with the going model's 56% on By The Book — that overweights connections against trip and course suitability.

CursorGuest House · 25%
Risk Khuskhas has already won this exact C&D and takes a high draw in a profile that favours the stands side.
pace map and whether a strong early gallop negates Guest House's hold-up profileForever Endless's unpublished OR and true abilitydraw impact refined for this 8-runner field rather than the full-sample 122-race stat
Guest House looks the best weighted chance on form, not price. He is 2–4 over today's trip, 2–5 on good ground, and arrives off a convincing 8f good-to-firm win at Yarmouth; the prior Newmarket July run reads much better than seventh of ten — beaten only a neck in a race Khuskhas won next time out. The 61 mark leaves useful headroom against rivals carrying more, Silvestre De Sousa is a positive booking, and draw three sits in the middle third that has won more often here than the low stalls where several rivals are camped.

The main danger is Khuskhas, not the market favourite narrative. He is a proven course-and-distance winner from draw seven in a race where high draws have overperformed, handles this ground, and is only two pounds better off than when winning here in June; I rate him close second rather than top because his Windsor fourth is slightly inferior to Guest House's current winning momentum, and the going model's 38% feels too bullish for a competitive eight-runner handicap. Napolian has the best figures but draw one is a serious negative at this track, and Royal Bodyguard is a solid each-way type without a clear edge over the front two.

official ratings for Alpha, Ibelieveicanfly and Blonde Over Bluepace map with three Joseph Patrick O'Brien runnersclass and trip of the 08-09 Curragh win
Alpha is the pick on substance, not the blanket 9-2 board. He is 1-1 at Curragh over 7f, 2-3 at the trip, and already beat Ibelieveicanfly by six lengths in a Curragh 7f on good ground in June; he followed that with a Class 1 Leopardstown win over this field type. Wayne Lordan and the lighter weight (211 vs 4241) are positives, and draw two is a minor negative in a five-runner race where high draws hit 43% historically — not enough to overturn proven course-and-distance form.

The main danger is Ibelieveicanfly: fresh Curragh winner, only a neck behind over 7f good to firm in July, and drawn widest in the favoured section. Dancing Destiny is the best of the Joseph Patrick O'Brien trio after a 0.2L Leopardstown Class 1 second but lacks Curragh form; Green Empress looks a 6f type on poor course figures; Blonde Over Blue is third-string on recent evidence. I rate Alpha at 34% — well below the going model’s 58% — because five-way pricing and a hot rival on the right draw keep this from a strong conviction claim.

Risk Good-to-soft may not suit as well as the Good ground he won on at Goodwood, and the next-day eighth over 8f hints stamina is not fully banked.
early pace map and whether Rogue Diplomat or a Balding runner force a true testGTS-specific form versus his Good-ground windraw 5 effectiveness in a 14-runner 7f versus the broad York draw sample
Lake Forest is the form horse most directly qualified for this test: he beat several of today's rivals when winning the Goodwood 7f Class 1 on good ground, with Rogue Diplomat second and Marvelman well held, and he has useful York course form (1-3). Draw 5 is workable in a 14-runner York 7f where low, mid and high are broadly balanced, and the Haggas/Fallon team is in strong recent form. He maps ahead of market favourite Notable Speech, who is top on OR but has been off 67 days, flopped over 6f last time, and has no course or going credentials here — short price is reputation, not proof over 7f on this ground.

The biggest danger is Ten Bob Tony: OR 121, proven at seven furlongs (4-10), and a Good-to-Soft winner at Epsom in Class 1 company, with a sensible mid draw. Flora Of Bermuda and Zavateri are next threats on recent 7f form and Murphy/Balding or low-draw consistency respectively, but Lake Forest has already shown he can put them away in comparable company, which is why he edges the verdict despite the going and stamina niggles.

Jazz Queen is my lean on evidence the market cannot replicate: a Chester 6f Class 2 second (0.5L, Good) on this stiff track, followed by respectable Class 2/3 six-furlong runs at Haydock and Doncaster. That is the clearest course-and-distance suitability in the field. She is fresher than Gladys Pugh and Bated Benevolence, more proven at six furlongs than Kentucky Rain (0-2 at trip, Beverley five-furlong win), and less dependent on a debut or single-run profile than Takaaful and Nicely. At roughly 9-2 her price aligns with a ~23% true chance rather than offering the false certainty implied by the shorter quotes elsewhere.

The main threat is The Can Can Queen on talent — OR 86 and a Newmarket July Class 1 third over six furlongs mark her the likely class act if rebounding from Ascot. Takaaful is the danger runner ignored at a single price: Boughey/Loughnane sending a debutant into a Chester Class 2 is a serious signal. My reservation on Jazz Queen is stall six in a seven-runner field where low draws take nearly half of historical wins, compounded by her Carlisle slow-start note; if she is ridden conservatively from a wide-ish berth, the Chester specialists behind could capitalize.

Words Of Truth is the pick on substance, not price. Top official rating (112), perfect going/course/course-and-distance records (1-1 across the board), and a Charlie Appleby profile that fits July sprint winners — including a prior win at this meeting over six furlongs on good to firm. The Newbury Class 1 success confirms the horse belongs at this level; Ascot third on good ground is respectable rather than a red flag. Draw three is neutral-to-fine in an eight-runner field where high-draw bias from larger samples should be discounted.

The main challenge is freshness: Prince Of India (0.3L sixth here on 11 July, high draw today) and Quinault (poor here last time but 2-3 course-and-distance) arrive in sharper recent race rhythm. Midnight Tango’s 1.1 quote looks disconnected from 13th-of-22 Ascot form, no course wins, and a long gap — I would not treat that market position as proof of ability. At a true ~30% chance versus 4.5 odds, Words Of Truth offers the clearest edge; Prince Of India is the chief danger if the favourite needs the run.

Risk Draw 1 fights Curragh 7f high-draw bias and Aidan O'Brien also runs Florida Bay off a fresh Leopardstown 7f Class 1 win.
OR marks for five of six runnerspace map with dual O'Brien/Cobden-style tactics unclearwhether 31-day break has left Giant Sequoia peaky vs fresher rivals
Giant Sequoia is the most convincing profile on paper: he has already won at Curragh over 7f on good-to-firm, with 1-2 course, course-and-distance, going and distance records, and Wayne Lordan aboard for the senior Aidan O'Brien string. That localized proof counts for more than the 1.1 quote, but it still makes him the likeliest winner in a field of recent Class 1 seven-furlong winners — not a 90% certainty. Nola Soul is the main danger on form: she has a strong Ascot seven-furlough Class 1 win on similar ground, perfect going and distance figures (2-2 at 7f, 1-1 on today's going), and draw 5 suits the Curragh seven-furlong high-bias pattern better than the favourite. Florida Bay is next: OR 95, he beat Nail House convincingly at Leopardstown over this trip and class, though he shares the low-draw drawback and may play second string to Giant Sequoia.

The biggest risk is overrating the market leader. At 1.1 the price assumes dominance; in a six-runner Class 1 with multiple winners, low draw, a fresh yardmate who won the same conditions recently, and Nola Soul's draw and seven-furlong credentials, Giant Sequoia's true chance is closer to one-in-three than nine-in-ten. CursorTarriance · 10%
Risk 24-runner variance and unknown draws in a race where high stalls have won 44% at this trip.
drawpace mapsoft-ground suitability vs Goodwood GF form
Tarriance maps cleanly onto this test: course-and-distance form is the strongest in the field (1-2 at York 14f, including a neck defeat over this trip in May), he was only a nose behind Hopewell Rock when that rival won over 14f at Goodwood last time, and Colin Keane arrives off a York winner on Good ground where course form mattered. Andrew Balding’s yard is reliable at this level, the 9-7 is workable in a deep handicap, and he should not be treated as a short-priced proof horse despite being near the head of the market.

The main reservation is that this is still a wide-open Class 2 with four Ian Williams runners, several Mullins/Haggas strings, and possible pace influences (Align The Stars, Furthur, Poetic Sound all marked). Hopewell Rock is the logical second — he beat Tarriance and much of this field at Goodwood — while Klassleader appeals on handicap terms after a York win and Haydock second over 14f. Without individual draws, any leader could face a messy trip; a poor stall or a softening surface that blunts his Goodwood/Fair ground profile would be the quickest way for Tarriance to run no better than a place.

Mi Sueno is the clearest form line in the race: he won this exact Newton Abbot 18.5f Good-to-Firm Class 5 handicap five weeks ago from 10-8, completing cleanly and beating several of today's rivals including Saucats (third), Son Of Hypnos (fourth) and Man Oh Man (well held). That is direct course-distance-going proof at this trip, with the lowest weight again in a field where jumping completion has been rewarded. Saucats is the main danger — three solid Newton Abbot 18f runs this summer, reliable hurdling, and only modest defeat behind Mi Sueno last time — while Man Oh Man's narrow second over this trip in June shows he can run a big figure when the run suits.

The biggest risk to Mi Sueno is regression off a career-low mark: a 73-rated winner in a race where several rivals carry more headroom (Saucats 82, Time Interval 99 on figures) can be vulnerable if the handicapper has him where he belongs. I strongly disagree with the going model on Time Interval at 52% — a 125-day break and April pull-up over hurdles at Stratford are major negatives for completion and fitness, and that caps him well below the model despite the Skelton/Sam Twiston-Davies slot. Bowensonfire is the most plausible winner on ability and profile: top OR (148), proven at trip and on good (1-5 both), and a fresh Galway second over 18f on good reads as trip-fit for 17f. Gordon Elliott's yard is in strong form and Jack Kennedy is a solid NH rider; the recent line is cleaner than the deeper form (7th/13th when stepped up). I do not read short-market logic into that — the case is ratings plus the latest staying chase effort, not price.

The main pushback is Putapoundinthejar, who arrives off a Galway good-ground chase win (16f, 1/20) with useful distance form (2-6) and a respectable 129 OR — the best current winning form in the field. I have him second but not first because Bowensonfire still looks materially better on the book and over a slightly longer, analogous Galway test. Eastmore is poor on good (0-9) including 8th over this trip/going at Cork; Kilgame's UR and layoff are chase negatives; Therellbguddaysyet is too inconsistent; Daddy Long Legs gets a Mullins/Hayes bump but OR 85 leaves him looking outclassed unless the mark is badly wrong. At 30% true win chance I would not treat this as a strong conviction race — the going model's 51% looks too bullish.

Navy Waters is the most trustworthy 12f profile here on what we know: fourth at this course and trip on good ground last time (beaten only 0.8L), fifth over 12f at Galway beaten half a length, and a prior Punchestown stamina run. Draw eight is neutral on Curragh 12f stats, OR 85 is workable without top weight, and W J Lee on a consistent stayer-type beats backing short prices on lightly exposed or unproven horses. Marazion tops the ratings but is 0-3 at Curragh with a flat sixth over CD; Vanir and Yousaynothingatall look strong on 10f Curragh form but are unproven at this trip.

The main doubt is the conversion record — Navy Waters keeps finishing near the front without winning. Nellcote is the main danger: a decisive Limerick 12f good-ground win off a light 8-13, from a yard with multiple runners and possible pace help, but an unknown OR makes her true chance hard to pin down. If Nellcote is handicapped near the mid-80s rather than punished for that win, she would overtake Navy Waters.

CursorAir Force One · 11%
Risk He is back at York only two days after an odds-on win, so a flat-back-up profile is the main danger.
confirmed pace map with four possible pacemakers in a 20-runner sprintwhether Tuesday's 5.5f York win leaves enough tank for 6f on Good to SoftStratusnine's true ground preference after Goodwood form on Good to Firm
Air Force One gets the nod on course-and-draw fit rather than market rank. He has the ideal low draw in a 20-runner York sprint where low stalls have a modest edge, proven York form including third over this exact six-furlong Class 2 handicap in July (beaten only 0.3L), and a 2-9 course record. Geoff Oldroyd's decision to quick-return him after Tuesday's York win signals confidence, and OR 90 leaves useful weight in a hot race. Stratusnine is the clear second: he won this same July York handicap from a wide draw and followed with a neck second at Goodwood, so his true chance is higher than 18.0 implies, but stall 13 is a meaningful downgrade today against Realign (draw 2, 1-1 on Good to Soft) and Coul Angel (York second, draw-proof here).

The biggest risk to Air Force One is the turnaround itself — winning at 1.0 on Tuesday over five and a half furlongs is not proof he will reproduce over six on softer ground 48 hours later, and Oldroyd also saddles Pocklington, which may split tactical focus. If the early pace is strong with multiple prominent runners, a hold-up type could swoop and compress the advantage low draws usually enjoy.

CursorSupreme Yeats · 27%
Risk His two Newton Abbot wins were over 26f, so this sharper 21.5f may suit course-speed rivals more than it suits him.
Handlethekettle's true fitness off only seven hurdle runsSoul Icon jumping reliability after recent unseatsearly pace pressure from Morning Mayhem or Handlethekettle
Supreme Yeats is the most trustworthy profile in an open Class 2: 2-2 at Newton Abbot on good, a recent 20f good-ground win at Bangor, and the Skelton/S Skelton axis that dominates the six-month ranks. He is not a short-price automaton — the 115 OR and 10-10 are fair rather than crushing — but course mastery, clean recent completion (no P/F/U), and proven stamina on this track outweigh the others on balance. American Sniper is the main danger: CD 1-1 here over 22f in May and useful distance figures, but he looks a notch below Yeats on current form after Uttoxeter and lacks the perfect course record.

The biggest threat is trip/pace shape, not the market. Morning Mayhem (1-2 at the course, narrowly beaten over 18f) and Handlethekettle (two good-ground 20f hurdle wins, including Class 2 at Worcester) both bring more tactical speed than a horse whose NA profile is built around 26f staying races; Zillow and Soul Icon are largely discounted for recent jumping failures and top-weight risk respectively. I would not treat Kitty Foyle's low OR as proof — she is 0-5 on good and her Kempton AW flop is a poor hurdle prep.

Emily Love has the strongest statistical good‑ground record (4‑8) and Killarney course form, but 76 days idle, a fall here in May, and a remote third when only three went to post at Punchestown cap her. Arqoob is the most convincing profile for this exact test: 2-2 at Newmarket (July), course-and-distance winner, and he beat Sixpack on this ground three weeks ago when winning over 12f here. The August analogue at this trip/class was won by this horse at a big price, which fits a progressive handicapper who is clearly comfortable on this track rather than a short-priced reputation pick. He shares a workable draw and weight with the main local rivals and arrives off a career-best run.

The main danger is Goblet Of Fire, not Bulletin. Henderson’s horse is the highest official rating, handles good ground, and was only 0.2L away in a Class 2 over this course and distance in July, so class may tell if the longer break and apprentice claim blunt his edge. Sixpack is the other live threat on bare ratings and James Owen’s strong recent record, but he has already finished behind Arqoob here this month and looks slightly less proven at this specific July venue.

Carmers is the right top pick on ability, not price: OR 112 is a clear ratings lead, he won the shared Down Royal 16f Good reference (Layfayette second, Dallas Star close fourth), and his 1-3 going / 1-3 distance record fits today. Draw three is neutral in a seven-runner field where high-draw bias is less reliable than the six-year sample. Layfayette is the main danger — fresher, Curragh CD 1-1, OR 106, and a recent win — but he was still beaten by Carmers on the most comparable ground.

The biggest risk is treating Carmers like a 90%-plus banker. Sixty-five days off, a poor Ascot 20f reappearance, and 0-0 at Curragh leave a fitness and course-local question that analog winners (SP 5.5–11) suggest this trip often throws up a viable alternative. If Kizlyar (@ 1.1) sets a strong gallop for stablemate Leinster, Carmers may need a career-best off the layoff to justify anything near 1.1; my 30% true win chance makes him favourite but not a slam dunk.

Bigalo is the most trustworthy form line in the field: three consecutive seconds at seven furlongs on good or good-to-firm, all within a length or so of the winner and at comparable Class 5/6 level. Draw six is neutral on Redcar’s mild low bias in an eleven-runner field, and he maps clearly ahead of the market-supported short prices — Right Up My Ali is badly out of form off a long break, Penny Arcade has been tailed off at shorter trips despite top weight on paper, and Maleny’s Jason Hart angle is real but still unexposed on debut. Amantha is the main danger: she won over this trip and going at Musselburgh and has twice finished behind Bigalo in the same races, but always further back and with a lower official rating, so Bigalo gets the narrow nod.

The biggest risk is profile rather than trip — Bigalo keeps running into trouble or finding one better at the line, which is exactly the sort of horse that markets underrate until it wins and overrate once it does. A Hart-ridden debutant (Maleny) or a well-handicapped Easterby newcomer could also steal this if the pace collapses or sets up for something unexposed; none of that is enough to pass Bigalo on known data, but it keeps…

Mojito Des Mottes gets the nod on profile rather than price: he is the most convincing recent hurdler in the field, beaten only a neck in a Class 2 at Ascot and progressive through his five runs before a Market Rasen PU that stewards linked to interference rather than a solo jumping meltdown. Pauling/Cobden is a solid NH combination, his 11-11 sits fairly at OR 118 in a race where several rivals carry bigger question marks, and 17f should be within range off 16f form. He lacks Newton Abbot course experience, but that matters less than Arctic Voyage’s last-course flop and the long layoffs/jumping faults elsewhere.

The biggest risk is that this remains a fragile six-runner handicap: Mojito is still lightly raced and has not proven he stays over 17f hurdles at Good to Firm, so a mistake or stamina doubt would open the door for Arctic Voyage, whose May win over this exact trip/course/class is the strongest course-and-distance card in the race despite June’s alarming 26L defeat. Lunar Orbit is the danger if Skelton has him fit off the long break—Harry Skelton’s booking over stablemate Charlus is the main signal—but 198 days off and a pulled-up in the form string keep him behind the…

AW suitability vs her 4-7 turf distance recordpace map and whether Wanderlust or Mwafaq force a true testdraw impact with only nine runners on standard
Pomme Pomme is the most convincing profile on fundamentals: 4-7 at today’s trip is far the best distance record in the field, she drops from a Pontefract Class 3 effort into Class 4 off 79 carrying 9-6 (5lb better treated than the 9-11 pair on the same mark), and draw 6 sits in the mid band that has won most often here. I am not treating Epictetus’s Sandown win or short price as proof — that was turf, his Lingfield run was good-to-firm turf too, and his 0-10 going stat on standard AW is a real downgrade despite the high draw fitting the slight stall bias.

Cloth Of Gold is the main danger: top OR 83, Newcastle AW 10f second, and a close Southwell reappearance read as a horse at the right level on synthetics. Kokanee’s June Lingfield AW win is the other live angle, but 48 days off, a low draw in a high-stall-skewed sample, and the class rise cap him below the top two for me in a genuinely open nine-runner handicap where no runner deserves much above ~17% true win chance.

CursorRaammee · 11%
Risk Four-run profile and 0-0 on Good To Soft mean the July GF course win may be overweighted at 4.6.
Raammee's ability on ground softer than Goodpace map with Dark Moon Rising/Double Parked possible forward pressureAccredit's official mark and race-fitness after 309 days
Raammee is the most reliable anchor: he has already won over York’s 10f in a 22-runner Class 2 handicap on the July card, with Castle Stuart third and several of today’s rivals well beaten behind him. Draw five is workable in a big field where low stalls help but do not dominate, and Roger Varian’s record supports a horse still lightly raced and open to progress. Ray Dawson knows the track, and the 9-12 weight looks fair rather than harsh against rivals carrying more such as Thunder Run and Erzindjan.

The main reservation is that today’s Good To Soft is not the Good/Firm surface of that breakthrough win, and a four-start career leaves little backup if softness blunts his action. Castle Stuart is the logical second choice: stall three fits the low-draw lean, he is 2nd and 3rd in his last two York 10f runs off a light 8-13 mark, and Al Aali’s Goodwood win marks him as the main form threat if the race turns into a test of current class rather than course knowledge.

CursorTeofil · 40%
Risk Four debutants—including a Paul Nolan runner—can land this without prior form, so the proven winner is far from bulletproof.
Official ratings for the fieldPace map / early speed over 16.5f at KillarneyPoint-to-point or bumper form for the unraced runners
Teofil is the only runner with a positive, relevant résumé on today's terms: he won over 16f on Good at Galway three weeks ago (1/13 at 4.5), and his prior Punchestown second over 16f on yielding ground confirms he stays this trip. That is a materially stronger profile than anyone else—Rokanako's Kilbeggan win came on yielding and was followed by a poor Tipperary run, while Farney Bridge, Loughtown and Lady Boudica have shown little or nothing. Bolger/Gleeson are respectable rather than hot (T14/J14 0-0), but the horse's course-and-distance/going suitability outweighs connection coldness here.

The biggest threat is not Rokanako's inconsistency but the four debuts in a nine-runner field. Emergency Man gets the nod as second mainly on Paul Nolan's strong six-month yard record (#155 on this card); Mystic Bridge (V T O'Brien) is the other debut worth respecting. With ORs unknown and no draw split at this field size, I would not push Teofil above 0.40 despite the going model's 42%—maiden-heavy races with unraced rivals routinely produce surprises even when one runner looks clearly best on form.

pace map and who leads over Chester's short run-inwhether Howth's listed OR124 is accurate versus the rest of this 0-85 bandfitness bounce after York flop for Midnight Rumble
Dino Bellagio is the only runner with a Chester win (1-1), from draw 2 on a course where local knowledge and position matter, and he carries a useful OR73 — roughly 6–8lb below the main block on 81-rated rivals. His 3-8 strike rate over today's trip and Donald McCain/Paul Mulrennan pairing fit a staying handicap more credibly than several shorter-trip novices in the field.

The biggest risk is that his overall profile is inconsistent (0-6 on good-to-soft, AW-heavy recent prep) and the yard's other runner Kuredu King has closer Chester 16f form and a going win; if McCain prioritises him or the race turns into a crawl, draw-one Midnight Rumble — third here over 16f in June beaten a neck — becomes the main danger.

pace map and run stylesconfirmed going on the daywhether Eve's Boy's recent poor runs reflect trip unsuitability or recoverable form
Woodleigh is the stand-out profile for this exact test: 2-2 at Redcar around 10f, 2-3 course and 2-3 at the trip, and a close fourth over 8f here 23 days ago. That is real course-and-distance suitability, not market noise. Draw two is neutral-to-slightly low on the published Redcar 10f bias, but in a nine-runner field that is a minor factor compared with his proven CD record. Roger Fell/Oisin McSweeney are not hot numerically, yet the horse’s local form is the clearest edge in the race.

The biggest danger is that this is still a open Class 5 handicap with several higher-rated rivals. Fille Imbassee brings a fresh Leicester 10f win on good-to-firm and high draw support; Bay Dream Believer is an in-form stayer with Jason Hart and strong distance stats; Sogniamo tops the weights on OR. Eve’s Boy at 1.1 looks far shorter than his true chance — no going, distance, course or CD form, 47 days off, and recent runs at 7f–8f ending in defeat — so I would not treat the favourite status as proof of winning ability here.

Mountbatten is the pick on a composite of draw, surface, and current profile. Stall five fits Lingfield AW’s high-draw lean at this trip, Luke Morris has recent Polytrack form including a Lingfield winner, and the horse arrives fresh off an Southwell AW victory with a near-miss at Yarmouth over 14f. The OR 66 mark looks workable in a modest Class 5, and 12f–14f form translates reasonably to 13f better than the pure sprinters in the field.

The main danger is Betelgeuse from draw six with tidy staying form — 2nd/3rd efforts at 14f–16f — though he lacks proven AW credentials and carries the weakest official rating with an inexperienced apprentice. Last Verse has class on OR 77 but draw one is a material negative here; Hebridean Nomad’s February second over this exact course and trip is the form line of the race, but six months off and a low draw make him hard to prefer over the two high-draw, race-fit contenders.

I am not treating short prices or top weights (Always Blue, Chesneys Charm) as proof; this is an open nine-runner handicap where no runner deserves much above ~0.17 true win chance.

**Eighth Immortal** is the clearest form/ratings case on what we know: OR 78 stands above Shemiyla Star (71) and everyone else is unrated, and both runs are useful — a close third over today’s 7f at Doncaster in Class 4 and another third at Chester. That is real competitiveness at this level, not a short-price illusion. Luke Morris is riding well on AW, and the horse looks the most likely to translate exposed ability to a win despite top weight.

The main doubt is structural, not ability. Lingfield’s 7f AW profile favours high stalls in big fields, so draw 2 is a meaningful headwind, and this is still only a third career start in a messy nursery-type heat where **Pirates Paradise** (5th on 7f debut in Class 2, strong draw 12), **Mount St** / **Starlight Bay** (capable yards, light weights, Starlight Bay widest), and unrated debutants could all outrun their prices. I have Eighth Immortal only around 15% true — top pick, but far from a strong staking race.

Draw bias at Redcar ~6f is essentially flat (low/mid/high all ~31–35%), so his high stall is not a meaningful negative; I am not elevating Liverpool Star or the market steam on Missmimi simply because prices have collapsed—Liverpool Star’s York ninth and mixed 5f/6f record do not support a true ~40%+ chance, while Missmimi’s edge is mainly Redcar CD (1–3) and a light 8st 13lb mark, with her latest work over 5f.

The main danger is Missmimi: she is the best-treated on ratings, knows this track, and if she stays 6f she can outrun a short price. Taygar (course-placed, light, low draw) and Ingleby Archie (Nottingham win, consistent) are the other live threats; Hover On The Wind’s hot 5f streak is less persuasive stepped up in trip and weight.

Draw 2 is neutral-to-favourable on Redcar’s flat 31/35/34 low-mid-high split, and his 1-2 at the course with 1-2 CD is the most relevant recent evidence at a trip he has already proven (Ripon 6f win in the mix). South Shore Island is the immediate danger on re-opposing form (second here, light 9-2, 7lb claim), while Drish Samphire’s Thirsk breakthrough adds volatility.
